source.version: Working paper dated March 2, 2026, by Xuekang Wu, Guy Aridor, and Artem Timoshenko; date and authors verified on PDF p. 1.
source.supplement_used: Appendices A-E in the same PDF, pp. 36-44 (printed pp. 35-43), and the complete Web Appendix A-D, PDF pp. 45-69 (printed WA-1 to WA-25), dated March 2, 2026.

studies.label: Field experiment 1: Armor Health healthcare logo contest (main study)
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individuals were randomized. The submission-level regressions cluster standard errors by designer (PDF p. 23, printed p. 22; Tables WA-C.1/WA-C.2 and WA-D.2/WA-D.3). Those regressions are excluded here because they adjust for submission date. The extracted descriptive output summaries do not report contrast standard errors.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 20 (printed p. 19), Section 4.1 and Table 1; assignment upon registration: PDF p. 19 (printed p. 18), Figure 4 notes
counts_source.quote:
A total of 440 designers registered for the experiment, with 292 designers submitting at least one logo (Table 1).
Open 105 70 (66.7% of registered) 499
Variation(1) 105 71 (67.6% of registered) 575
Variation(4) 120 76 (63.3% of registered) 550
Blind 110 75 (68.2% of registered) 575

arms.name: Variation(1)
arms.description: Brief plus a gallery of one AI-generated variation for each of the 60 exemplars, shown with the original exemplars' click-attractiveness ratings; the paper's focal treatment arm

arms.name: Variation(4)
arms.description: Brief plus a gallery of four AI-generated variations for each of the 60 exemplars, shown with the originals' ratings; included to test whether more variations per exemplar help

arms.name: Open
arms.description: Brief plus a gallery of the 60 original human-made exemplars (from the brand's 2019 private contest) with their quality ratings

arms.name: Blind
arms.description: Contest brief only, no exemplars or variations

studies.task: Professional freelance designers created logos for Armor Health, a healthcare brand, in a contest aimed at attracting clicks in online advertising.

ai_tool.name: FLUX.1-dev fine-tuned with Logo LoRA and Optimization LoRA; prompts combine a creative-brief summary with a JoyCaption description of each exemplar. Researchers supplied the generated variations in galleries.
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 10), Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF p. 33 (printed p. 32), reference: Black Forest Labs (2024, August). FLUX.1-dev (model card). The year identifies the base-model reference, not the experiment date.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is stated in the paper or its appendices.

estimates.outcome: Alignment with leading exemplars, all submissions
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Maximum alignment of each submitted logo with the 12 original leading exemplars. Composite of motif Dice overlap and motif text-embedding similarity, color-set overlap, color-moment and atmospheric-style measures, and scene-graph and Hu-moment measures. The appendix describes averaging standardized alignment measures. automated_score is an approximate codebook category for this computed index, not a creativity-judging model. Higher values indicate stronger alignment with supplied exemplars, not similarity among different participants.
estimates.treatment_arm: Variation (arm composition not stated; possibly Variation(1) and Variation(4) pooled)

stats.difference_is: Variation minus Blind, as printed in the Variation column under Delta vs. Blind.

PDF p. 44 (printed p. 43), Table E.3 notes

sources.locator: PDF p. 42 (printed p. 41), Appendix E.2, alignment construction
sources.quote: For each submission, we com- pute its alignment measures with the 12 original exemplars and then take the maximum as the submission’s alignment score.

estimates.notes: Appendix E labels the AI column Variation without stating whether it contains Variation(1), Variation(4), or both. The arm label follows the reconciled form and does not assert pooling. The table does not print analysis-specific designer counts or arm output counts, so n_treatment, n_control, n_total, and n_units remain null. Unadjusted whole-sample descriptive result, retained under construct other. The reported SDs describe dispersion across submissions; no contrast SE, CI, test statistic, or p-value is printed. se_basis is not_reported because no inferential uncertainty for this contrast is given. The difference is transcribed from the table.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Submission prevalence of the shield feature; binary output attribute, reported as a proportion. Appendix E uses ChatGPT 5.2 for motif/color extraction and scene graphs for spatial relationships. automated_score is an approximate label for automated feature extraction, not an automated creativity judgment. Only the Submissions columns are used; Quality Cor. and the Exemplar columns are not treatment-effect statistics.
estimates.treatment_arm: Variation (arm composition not stated; possibly Variation(1) and Variation(4) pooled)

The originality regressions additionally select outputs using post-treatment quality: top 50 or 100 per condition, or top 200 or 400 across conditions. See PDF pp. 23-24 and 27 (printed pp. 22-23 and 26), Figures 6 and 9A, and PDF pp. 63-64 (printed WA-19 to WA-20), Tables WA-C.2 and WA-C.4. open_items: No unadjusted full-sample quality or originality contrast is printed for either field experiment. Their reported regressions control for post-assignment submission date; these require an unadjusted or baseline-only reanalysis before eligible effect extraction under rule 5.

Appendix E does not identify whether Variation means Variation(1), Variation(4), or their combination. Treatment-arm identity, corresponding participant count, and per-arm output counts for Tables E.2/E.3 require clarification; pooling is not assumed.
Table E.3 prints output-level SDs but no participant-level SDs or inferential uncertainty for the arm contrasts. Table E.2 prints only feature prevalences/means, with no arm uncertainty.

Submission depth lacks arm means, SDs, numerical test statistics, degrees of freedom, and p-values. Study 1 supplies only a pooled mean and qualitative pairwise-test statement; Study 2 has no fluency-specific test. Do not derive arm means by dividing submission totals by designer counts.

Study 2 says it follows the Section 4 design but does not separately restate assignment timing. Registered arm counts are used as randomized counts following that design; analyzed counts include only those submitting a logo.
